For me, a film is something that you watch in a cinema. A dark room, a huge screen, and two hundred people who laugh at the same moment. Last month I saw an old film that I had watched many times on TV, and at the cinema it was a completely different film. I noticed details that I had never seen. At home, I always look at my phone. In the cinema, the phone stays in my pocket. So when somebody asks me for a recommendation, I always say the same thing. Go out, buy a ticket, and turn off your phone.

I love films, but I prefer series, and I prefer my sofa. A good series is like a long novel. You live with the characters for weeks. The last one that I watched was about a family whose restaurant was in trouble, and I felt that I knew every person in that kitchen. A film gives you two hours. A series gives you a whole world. And at home, I can stop, go back, and watch a scene again in English with subtitles. Honestly, that is how I learned half of my English.
